A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, research questions and core analyses. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C support a reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original optimizer experiments on synthetic data, MNIST, Dominoes and four subgroup-robustness benchmarks, with additional results in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds subgroup-robustness results under broader hyperparameter sweeps and larger batch sizes.

M1.justification: The GD, signGD and Adam update rules, network formulations and losses are retained. The revisions concern theoretical assumptions, experimental settings and implementation disclosures, without introducing a new algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: The same Gaussian, patched-MNIST, MNIST-CIFAR, Waterbirds, CelebA, MultiNLI, CivilComments and Boolean-feature coverage remains. The additional Dominoes correlation strengths and Boolean-feature variants already appeared in v1's appendix. Larger batches and broader tuning introduce no new task or data population.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain GD/SGD and Adam, signGD in the toy analysis, and the linear-predictor reference in the MNIST experiment. V2 evaluates additional optimizer configurations without adding or removing comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix B.4 adds a substantially different subgroup evaluation: batches of 512 for Waterbirds/MultiNLI and 1024 for CelebA/CivilComments, with broader learning-rate, momentum and weight-decay sweeps. V1's batches of 128 for images and 32 for language remain in the smaller-batch comparison. This changes the main reported evaluation settings rather than merely documenting the original experiments.

E4.justification: New Figure 10 systematically examines optimizer sensitivity to learning rate, weight decay and momentum across all four subgroup benchmarks. Tables 13–14 also allow comparison across larger- and smaller-batch configurations. These substantially extend the existing Gaussian stochasticity and Boolean initialization analyses.

E5.justification: V2 reports five independent runs for the new larger-batch image experiments, whereas v1's subgroup experiments used four. The retained smaller-batch results and new language results use four runs. This concerns the new experimental configuration, not an established increase in runs for the original results; the existing uncertainty-reporting style remains.

E6.justification: V1 Table 13 is retained unchanged as v2 Table 14, while new Table 13 and Figure 10 add results under different settings. For example, new CelebA worst-group accuracy is 67.56 for SGD versus 77.22 for Adam, but average accuracy is 93.74 versus 90.89. Adam also has lower average accuracy on CivilComments, 85.73 versus 86.68. These are new comparisons, not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 extends Theorem 5's proof with bounded-gradient, norm-growth and integration arguments establishing directional convergence. Theorem 6 replaces vanishing initialization with the explicit bound sup_k ||w_k,0|| < eta/2 and adds first-step and recursive reasoning. These refine existing results; the remaining theoretical framework is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: contrasting SGD's simplicity bias with Adam's richer feature learning, explaining this theoretically in synthetic settings, and demonstrating benefits under spurious correlations. The added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 explicitly qualifies the connection between the gradient-flow theorem and discrete-time GD: the theorem is predictive of the observed small-step behavior. This sharpens an applicability distinction previously left implicit in the discussion. Appendix C's broader limitations and cautions about simplicity bias remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents GPU hardware and dataset licenses, and specifies MNIST's 14-by-14 resolution, width 64, batch size 64, initialization and fixed output weights. It also supplies tuning grids and epoch budgets for the new subgroup experiments. The MNIST additions are disclosures, not evidence of a changed implementation.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Mulayoff, Michaeli and Soudry's work on the implicit bias of minima stability, with a brief description. The broader positioning and novelty discussion remain stable. Conversion from author-year to numbered citations does not constitute additional related-work coverage.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized edits to the abstract, optimizer terminology and proof exposition, and organizes Appendix B.4 into main results and smaller-batch results. The overall section sequence and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted into NeurIPS style, with different typography, a narrower text area, resized displays and redistributed figures and tables. V2 adds the 16-panel Figure 10 and a new subgroup-results table, redraws Figure 2 with the new results, and relocates retained appendix displays.

improvement.justification: Broader optimizer tuning makes the subgroup comparisons more informative, while the added proof arguments and implementation details improve precision and reproducibility. These benefits are tempered by an unresolved reporting mismatch: Section 4.4 still claims better average accuracy for Adam, although new Table 13 shows lower averages on CelebA and CivilComments. The revision provides a limited net improvement while retaining the original scientific scope.
